Subject: Sudden latency / 5xx spike this morning — we need immediate help

Hi Karthik,

We started seeing a sustained latency spike and a 5xx error increase around 07:30 PT this morning. Our dashboards show p95 latency crossing 1.7s (normal ~350ms) and a steady queueing backlog for our reserved endpoints — this is directly affecting downstream transaction validation. Attached is a small CSV with the top 10 error timestamps and request IDs.

Can Redwood provide an immediate mitigation (burst capacity or a temporary fallback to a higher-throughput variant)? We are on a reserved capacity plan and this gap is causing failed payments. We need an estimate for how long remediation will take and whether you can authorize any short-term capacity credit.

Please escalate — CC'ing Rajiv (CTO) for visibility.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Head of Platform Reliability
PrimeBank

Forwarding PrimeBank's alert — they report p95 ~1.7s and increased 5xx. Immediate ask: confirm whether their reserved pool is saturated, whether noisy neighboring workloads are spilling, and whether automatic KV/prefix caching is functioning for their routes.

Ops, please run headroom and queue depth checks for PrimeBank's reserved pool (pool id RB-PB-DBL4821) and prioritize any fast rollback to a compatible fallback model if throughput is constrained. If we need burst capacity, call out required GPU hours and I will escalate for exec authorization.

Karthik

---Original message below---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T08:36:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden latency / 5xx spike this morning — PrimeBank (ops findings)

Karthik / team,

Quick readout from the cluster: their dedicated GPU pool is at 98% utilization across the 4 nodes assigned (concurrent KV cache pressure and longer sequence lengths due to a new inference path they rolled out at 07:00). We see sustained queueing in the scheduler and a small but growing number of token OOMs which trigger 502s. Noisy neighbor influence appears minimal — this is consistent with an actual delta in PrimeBank traffic profile.

What we can do immediately:
- Enable temporary autoscale burst: +2 GPU cards in the pool (estimated 6 hours to provision warm capacity), OR
- Route a subset (10-15%) of high-latency traffic to the warmed quantized variant (Q4_compatible) with slightly degraded quality but much higher throughput (can be done in ~12 minutes), OR
- Apply aggressive prefix caching for identical early tokens (risk: cache hit regressions for dynamic prompts).

Estimate: autoscale burst reduces p95 to ~400-500ms; routing to quantized variant reduces p95 to ~500-700ms. Both reduce 5xx substantially.

I recommend routing 15% to quantized variant immediately while we request exec approval for a +2 GPU burst for 12 hours. Need Karthik to escalate for spend approval.

Marcus
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Exec escalation: authorization request for short-term burst (PrimeBank DBL-4821)

Naomi / Laura — I need an urgent spend/credit authorization to provision a short-term burst for PrimeBank's dedicated pool. Customer impact: failed payment validations, revenue-impacting, and CTO on the thread. Details: +2 A100 equivalent GPUs for up to 12 hours. Estimated incremental cost: $7,500 (hardware + setup). Business ask: approve one-time charge / credit and sign a temporary amendment (DocuSign) to cover the burst.

Customer will accept partial routing to the quantized model while we stand up capacity, but they want our commitment to a hard SLA until usage normalizes. Attaching our capacity runbook for outreach notes.

DocuSign draft: docusign-burst-amendment.docx (needs legal sign-off, but we need a quick OK to proceed).

Karthik

Attachments: capacity_runbook.pdf, docusign-burst-amendment.docx

Sarah, Rajiv — quick update and plan of action:
1) We're routing 15% of your traffic to the Q4_compatible quantized variant now (this reduces p95 and 5xx quickly). Expect initial improvement in ~15 minutes.
2) Naomi approved a one-time short-term burst (+2 GPUs) for up to 12 hours; we're provisioning now. Estimated warm time ~6 hours but routing + quantized fallback should stabilize customer-facing latency sooner.
3) We're preparing a short amendment for the burst and a contingency credit if the issue isn't resolved in the next 12 hours. Marcus and ops are monitoring in real time and will share telemetry.

We will follow up with a postmortem and capacity plan to prevent recurrence (model variant recommendations, KV cache tuning, and a pre-warm playbook).

Appreciate the quick flag — we'll keep you updated every 30 minutes until stable.

—Karthik
